 AND

THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION INDERGARH, DISTRICT DATIA (MADHYA  PRADESH)
 .
 (BY MR. P.P.S VAZEETA - DY. PUBLIC PROSECUTOR)
 This application coming on for Admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail relating to Crime No. 10 of 2024 registered at Police Station Indergarh, District Datia (M.P.) for the offence under Section 420, 120, 467 and 34 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
Applicant is having aged about 68 years and is under custody since 16.03.2024.
Investigation stands completed by filing of the charge sheet and further custodial interrogation of the applicant may not be required.

It is further argued that as per prosecution story, a registered sale deed was executed by the applicant-accused in favour of complainant in the year 2011 and thereafter mutation has also been done in favour of complainant and after elapse of 13 years, present FIR has been registered on the basis of KCC loan taken by the applicant-accused.

It is further submitted that applicant- accused is only liable to pay the KCC loan, therefore, there is no liability on the Karan Singh Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88724089/

. The applicant is permanent resident of District Datia (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, h e prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
P e r contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the respondent/State vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for dismissal of present bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary available on record.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

5) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6 ) The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (LJ*)
